answer: A verifiable random function, seeded at each epoch's dawn, draws the grading jury with seat odds proportional to locked stake — a trellis of bonded weight, never a headcount. An attacker cannot pre-pick which clones get seated; to swing any verdict they must out-bond the honest majority of total staked value. A thousand hollow accounts holding only dust draw near-zero seats, so controlling an outcome costs real capital equal to the entire honest stake pool — a price that scales with the network, not with the count of fake identities.
